content.text: The excerpt covers parasitic disease of the biliary passages and portal vein, then extensive diseases of the pancreas, including anatomy, physiology, causes, symptoms, diagnosis, and historical treatments for pancreatitis, carcinoma, degeneration, hemorrhage, duct obstruction, and cysts. It proceeds to acute, chronic, tuberculous, cancerous, and infantile peritonitis, emphasizing pain, distension, constipation, fever, ascites, adhesions, abscesses, and perforation. Treatments described include diet, opium, surgery, drainage, and supportive care. It concludes with tabes mesenterica—tuberculosis of mesenteric glands—its pathology, presentation in children, poor prognosis, prevention, and nutritional palliation. Cases and observations are reported from Brazil, England, Philadelphia, Washington, New York, Vermont, Bellevue Hospital, and other locations.
